--- Attachment ---
CVPR 2026 Poster Presentation Guidelines

Thank you for your interest in presenting at CVPR 2026. This document provides detailed guidelines for poster presenters, including poster board dimensions, layout recommendations, setup instructions, and best practices. Please read this information carefully to ensure a smooth and successful presentation experience.

1. Poster Board Specifications

Poster presenters will be provided with a dedicated space on a poster board for display during their assigned session. Please adhere strictly to the following dimensions:

- Maximum Poster Size: 42 inches (width) x 36 inches (height)
- Orientation: Landscape only (horizontal layout)

Each poster board will be labeled with your assigned poster number. Presenters must ensure that their posters do not exceed the maximum allowable size, as oversized posters may not fit on the boards and could impede neighboring displays.

2. Materials and Mounting

Poster boards are constructed of sturdy foam core material and will be supplied with push pins or Velcro strips for mounting. You do not need to bring your own mounting materials unless you prefer a specific type.

- Allowed mounting methods: Push pins (provided), Velcro strips (provided)
- Not allowed: Tape, glue, staples, or any adhesive that could damage the boards

Please ensure that your poster can be easily affixed using the provided materials. If your poster requires special support, contact the conference secretariat in advance.

3. Layout Recommendations

To maximize the impact and readability of your poster, we recommend the following layout tips:

A. Title Section

- Place the title of your paper prominently at the top of the poster.
- Include author names and affiliations beneath the title.
- Use font sizes large enough to be readable from at least 5 feet away (suggested: Title ≥ 72 pt; Authors/Affiliations ≥ 48 pt).

B. Content Organization

Organize your content into clear sections such as:

- Abstract
- Introduction
- Methods
- Results
- Discussion
- Conclusion
- References (if applicable)
- Acknowledgments (optional)

Use headers to separate sections and make navigation easy for viewers.

C. Visuals and Figures

- Use high-resolution images, diagrams, graphs, or tables wherever possible.
- Ensure all visuals are clearly labeled and legible.
- Avoid clutter—leave sufficient white space between sections.
- When presenting data, use color judiciously for clarity but ensure accessibility for colorblind attendees.

D. Text Guidelines

- Keep text concise; avoid long paragraphs.
- Use bullet points where appropriate.
- Font size for body text should be no smaller than 24 pt.
- Choose clear fonts such as Arial, Helvetica, or Times New Roman.

E. Contact Information

Include your email address or other contact details at the bottom right corner so interested attendees can follow up after the session.

4. Printing Specifications

To ensure quality presentation, please note:

- Posters must be printed on paper or fabric that is lightweight enough to mount easily but durable enough to withstand handling.
- Glossy or matte finishes are acceptable; avoid highly reflective surfaces that cause glare under lighting.
- Do not laminate posters as this can make them difficult to mount securely.

If printing locally in Vancouver, several print shops offer expedited poster printing services. We recommend contacting them well in advance of the conference dates.

5. Poster Session Logistics

A. Setup and Removal

Presenters are responsible for installing their posters during designated setup periods:

- Setup times: [To be announced closer to conference date; typically morning of session]
- Removal times: Posters must be taken down promptly after your session concludes.

Any posters left behind after sessions will be discarded by conference staff unless prior arrangements are made.

B. Presenter Attendance

At least one author must be present at the poster during official session hours to discuss the work with attendees and answer questions.

C. Poster Numbering

Your assigned poster number will be sent via email approximately two weeks before the conference along with final scheduling details. Please include this number on your poster in the top left corner for identification purposes.

6. Accessibility Considerations

CVPR is committed to providing an inclusive environment for all participants. To ensure accessibility:

- Use high contrast colors between background and text/figures.
- Avoid reliance solely on color to convey information—use patterns or labels where possible.
- Provide alt-text descriptions for key visuals if supplementary materials are distributed digitally.
- Ensure all text is readable from a reasonable distance (at least 5 feet).

If you require additional accommodations or have specific accessibility needs regarding your poster display, contact cvpr2026@conference.org no later than one month before the event.

7. Digital Poster Submission (Optional)

In addition to physical posters, presenters may upload a digital version of their poster prior to the conference via our online platform. Instructions for submission will be distributed in May 2026.

Digital posters should match physical content and layout as closely as possible and be submitted in PDF format.

8. Best Practices for Effective Posters

A successful poster communicates your research clearly and efficiently even in a crowded environment:

A. Design Simplicity

Aim for clarity rather than complexity—viewers typically spend less than five minutes per poster.

B. Visual Hierarchy

Highlight key findings using larger fonts or bold colors so they stand out immediately.

C. Interactive Elements

If desired, QR codes linking to supplementary materials (e.g., videos, datasets) may be included at the bottom of your poster.

D. Practice Your Pitch

Prepare a brief oral summary (~2 minutes) of your work for visitors who stop by your poster.

E. Professional Conduct

Be respectful of neighboring presenters and maintain professional interactions with attendees at all times.

9. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q1: Can I use portrait orientation?
A1: No; only landscape orientation is permitted due to board configuration constraints.

Q2: What happens if my poster exceeds the stated dimensions?
A2: Oversized posters may not fit on the boards and could obstruct adjacent displays; please ensure compliance with size restrictions.

Q3: Are there restrictions on colors or branding?
A3: No specific restrictions beyond those noted under accessibility considerations; institutional logos are permitted but should not dominate the design.

Q4: Will electrical outlets or tables be available?
A4: No electrical outlets or tables are provided at individual poster stations; please plan accordingly if demonstrating hardware/software separately.

Q5: Is it possible to change my assigned session?
A5: Session assignments are finalized based on program constraints; requests may be considered only under exceptional circumstances before May 15th, 2026.

10. Contact Information

For further questions about poster presentations, logistics, or accessibility needs, please contact:

CVPR 2026 Secretariat  
Email: cvpr2026@conference.org  
Phone: +1 (604) XXX XXXX  
Website: https://cvpr2026.org/

We look forward to welcoming you to CVPR 2026 and appreciate your efforts in preparing an engaging and informative poster presentation!

Journal of AI Ethics Author Guidelines 2025

Introduction
The Journal of AI Ethics is a peer-reviewed publication dedicated to advancing scholarship on the ethical, societal, and philosophical implications of artificial intelligence (AI). The journal welcomes interdisciplinary submissions that engage with both technical and conceptual dimensions of AI ethics, including works that integrate empirical research, theoretical analysis, and practical case studies. We encourage contributions from researchers in computer science, philosophy, law, social sciences, and related fields.

These guidelines are intended to assist authors in preparing manuscripts for submission. Please read them carefully before submitting your work.

1. Scope of the Journal
The Journal of AI Ethics publishes original research articles, review papers, case studies, commentaries, and perspectives on topics including but not limited to:

- Algorithmic fairness and bias
- Explainability and transparency in AI systems
- Alignment problems and value specification
- Responsible AI development and deployment
- Human-AI interaction and collaboration
- Privacy, data governance, and surveillance
- Societal impact and public policy considerations
- Philosophical foundations of AI ethics (e.g., moral agency, autonomy)
- Technical approaches to ethical challenges in AI
- Interdisciplinary analyses combining technical and philosophical perspectives

We explicitly welcome submissions that bridge technical and philosophical analysis, such as those addressing the alignment problem from both computational and normative viewpoints.

2. Manuscript Types
We accept the following types of manuscripts:

a) Original Research Articles (5000–9000 words)
Substantial contributions reporting novel findings or methodologies with clear relevance to AI ethics. May include empirical studies, technical analyses, or philosophical arguments.

b) Review Papers (6000–10,000 words)
Comprehensive overviews of a particular area within AI ethics. Should critically evaluate existing literature and propose future directions.

c) Case Studies (3000–6000 words)
Detailed examinations of real-world instances involving ethical issues in AI. Must provide context, analysis, and implications.

d) Commentaries & Perspectives (2000–4000 words)
Shorter pieces offering critical commentary on recent developments or ongoing debates in AI ethics.

e) Letters to the Editor (up to 1500 words)
Brief communications regarding previously published articles or emerging issues.

3. Manuscript Preparation

a) Formatting
- Manuscripts must be submitted in English.
- Use standard A4 or US Letter size with 1-inch margins.
- Font: Times New Roman or Arial; size: 12 pt; double-spaced.
- Pages should be numbered consecutively.
- Include line numbers for ease of review.

b) Structure
Original Research Articles should contain the following sections:
1. Title Page
2. Abstract (250–300 words)
3. Keywords (4–6 relevant terms)
4. Introduction
5. Methods/Approach (for technical or empirical work; may include philosophical methodology)
6. Results/Findings/Analysis
7. Discussion
8. Conclusion
9. References

Review Papers should follow a similar structure but may adapt sections according to topic coverage.

Case Studies should include background/context, description of the case, ethical analysis, outcomes/implications, and references.

Commentaries/Perspectives should have a concise introduction and focused argument/discussion.

c) Title Page Information
Include:
- Full manuscript title
- Authors’ full names and institutional affiliations
- Corresponding author’s contact information (email address)
- Word count (excluding references)

d) Abstract & Keywords
Provide a structured abstract summarizing aims, methods/approach, main findings/arguments, and conclusions. List 4–6 keywords reflecting core topics.

e) Figures & Tables
Figures/tables should be embedded within the manuscript at appropriate locations and accompanied by descriptive captions. All figures/tables must be cited in the text.

f) Equations & Code Snippets
If relevant (particularly for technical content), equations should be formatted clearly using LaTeX or Word equation editor. Code snippets should use monospace font and be well-commented; longer code can be provided as supplementary material.

g) Citations & References
Use APA 7th edition citation style throughout.
References must be comprehensive and up-to-date.
Where possible, cite primary sources rather than reviews.

h) Footnotes & Endnotes
Use footnotes sparingly for clarifications only; avoid excessive annotation.

i) Language & Style
Manuscripts should be written clearly for an interdisciplinary audience.
Avoid jargon where possible; define technical terms upon first use.
Authors are encouraged to balance technical rigor with accessibility for readers outside their primary discipline.

4. Ethical Considerations

a) Originality & Plagiarism
Submissions must represent original work not published elsewhere nor under consideration by another journal. All manuscripts are screened for plagiarism using automated tools.

b) Conflicts of Interest
Authors must disclose any potential conflicts of interest—financial or otherwise—in a dedicated section at the end of the manuscript prior to references.

c) Data Sharing & Reproducibility
For empirical or computational work:
- Describe datasets used; provide access details if publicly available.
- If proprietary data is used, explain access restrictions.
- Computational experiments should be described sufficiently for reproducibility; share code where feasible via repositories such as GitHub or institutional platforms.
- For studies involving human subjects or sensitive data, indicate ethical approval status from relevant review boards.

d) Human Subjects & Sensitive Content
Research involving human participants must comply with institutional guidelines and include statements regarding informed consent and ethical approval.

5. Submission Process

a) Online Submission System
Manuscripts must be submitted via our online platform at https://journalofaie.org/submit  
Create an account using your institutional email address.

b) Cover Letter Requirements
Include a cover letter addressed to the Editorial Team summarizing your manuscript’s contribution to AI ethics and its interdisciplinary relevance where applicable.

c) Supplementary Material
Authors may submit supplementary files such as datasets, code repositories, appendices, or multimedia content (audio/video demonstrations). Indicate these files clearly during submission.

d) Preprints Policy
We allow submission of manuscripts previously posted as preprints provided this is disclosed in the cover letter with a link to the preprint server.

6. Peer Review Process

a) Review Model  
The Journal operates double-blind peer review: identities of authors and reviewers are concealed during evaluation.

b) Review Criteria  
Manuscripts are evaluated based on originality, significance to AI ethics discourse, methodological rigor (technical/philosophical), clarity of presentation, interdisciplinary integration (where relevant), quality of argumentation/evidence, ethical compliance, and relevance to journal scope.

c) Revision & Decision  
Authors will receive reviewer feedback within 8 weeks of submission on average. Decisions may be:
- Accept without revision  
- Minor revision  
- Major revision  
- Reject  

Revised manuscripts must address reviewer comments point-by-point in an accompanying response letter.

7. Post-Acceptance Procedures

a) Copyright & Licensing  
Upon acceptance, authors will sign a publication agreement granting the Journal non-exclusive rights to publish the article under a Creative Commons Attribution license unless otherwise negotiated.

b) Proofs  
Authors will receive galley proofs for final correction prior to publication; only typographical errors may be corrected at this stage.

c) Publication Fees  
As an open-access journal committed to equitable dissemination, there are no mandatory article processing charges for accepted papers in 2025 due to grant support from sponsoring institutions. Voluntary donations are welcome but not required.

8. Special Issues & Thematic Calls

The Journal periodically publishes special issues on emerging themes in AI ethics (e.g., “Alignment Problems: Technical Approaches & Moral Foundations”). Authors interested in contributing to special issues should consult current calls at https://journalofaie.org/calls-for-papers

9. Contact Information

Questions about submissions may be directed to editorial@journalofaie.org

10. Checklist Before Submission

Please ensure you have:
- Followed all formatting requirements  
- Included all required sections  
- Provided complete references  
- Disclosed conflicts of interest  
- Described data/code sharing procedures if applicable  
- Included a cover letter summarizing your manuscript’s fit with journal scope  

11. Example Topics Bridging Technical & Philosophical Analysis

To further clarify scope for interdisciplinary submissions—including alignment problems—the following examples illustrate suitable topics:
- Formal models for specifying moral values in machine learning systems alongside normative critique.
- Empirical investigations into unintended consequences of reinforcement learning agents with philosophical discussion of agency/responsibility.
- Case studies on real-world failures in algorithmic alignment accompanied by moral analysis.
- Proposals for integrating ethical theories into reward design mechanisms with theoretical justification.
If uncertain whether your topic fits journal scope, please contact us prior to submission.

Thank you for considering the Journal of AI Ethics as a venue for your work! We look forward to your contribution toward responsible innovation in artificial intelligence.

Case Studies should include background/context, description of the case, ethical analysis, outcomes/implications, and references.

Commentaries/Perspectives should have a concise introduction and focused argument/discussion.

c) Title Page Information
Include:
- Full manuscript title
- Authors’ full names and institutional affiliations
- Corresponding author’s contact information (email address)
- Word count (excluding references)

d) Abstract & Keywords
Provide a structured abstract summarizing aims, methods/approach, main findings/arguments, and conclusions. List 4–6 keywords reflecting core topics.

e) Figures & Tables
Figures/tables should be embedded within the manuscript at appropriate locations and accompanied by descriptive captions. All figures/tables must be cited in the text.

f) Equations & Code Snippets
If relevant (particularly for technical content), equations should be formatted clearly using LaTeX or Word equation editor. Code snippets should use monospace font and be well-commented; longer code can be provided as supplementary material.

g) Citations & References
Use APA 7th edition citation style throughout.
References must be comprehensive and up-to-date.
Where possible, cite primary sources rather than reviews.

h) Footnotes & Endnotes
Use footnotes sparingly for clarifications only; avoid excessive annotation.

i) Language & Style
Manuscripts should be written clearly for an interdisciplinary audience.
Avoid jargon where possible; define technical terms upon first use.
Authors are encouraged to balance technical rigor with accessibility for readers outside their primary discipline.

4. Ethical Considerations

a) Originality & Plagiarism
Submissions must represent original work not published elsewhere nor under consideration by another journal. All manuscripts are screened for plagiarism using automated tools.

b) Conflicts of Interest
Authors must disclose any potential conflicts of interest—financial or otherwise—in a dedicated section at the end of the manuscript prior to references.

c) Data Sharing & Reproducibility
For empirical or computational work:
- Describe datasets used; provide access details if publicly available.
- If proprietary data is used, explain access restrictions.
- Computational experiments should be described sufficiently for reproducibility; share code where feasible via repositories such as GitHub or institutional platforms.
- For studies involving human subjects or sensitive data, indicate ethical approval status from relevant review boards.

d) Human Subjects & Sensitive Content
Research involving human participants must comply with institutional guidelines and include statements regarding informed consent and ethical approval.

5. Submission Process

a) Online Submission System
Manuscripts must be submitted via our online platform at https://journalofaie.org/submit  
Create an account using your institutional email address.

b) Cover Letter Requirements
Include a cover letter addressed to the Editorial Team summarizing your manuscript’s contribution to AI ethics and its interdisciplinary relevance where applicable.

c) Supplementary Material
Authors may submit supplementary files such as datasets, code repositories, appendices, or multimedia content (audio/video demonstrations). Indicate these files clearly during submission.

d) Preprints Policy
We allow submission of manuscripts previously posted as preprints provided this is disclosed in the cover letter with a link to the preprint server.

6. Peer Review Process

a) Review Model  
The Journal operates double-blind peer review: identities of authors and reviewers are concealed during evaluation.

b) Review Criteria  
Manuscripts are evaluated based on originality, significance to AI ethics discourse, methodological rigor (technical/philosophical), clarity of presentation, interdisciplinary integration (where relevant), quality of argumentation/evidence, ethical compliance, and relevance to journal scope.

c) Revision & Decision  
Authors will receive reviewer feedback within 8 weeks of submission on average. Decisions may be:
- Accept without revision  
- Minor revision  
- Major revision  
- Reject  

Revised manuscripts must address reviewer comments point-by-point in an accompanying response letter.

7. Post-Acceptance Procedures

a) Copyright & Licensing  
Upon acceptance, authors will sign a publication agreement granting the Journal non-exclusive rights to publish the article under a Creative Commons Attribution license unless otherwise negotiated.

b) Proofs  
Authors will receive galley proofs for final correction prior to publication; only typographical errors may be corrected at this stage.

c) Publication Fees  
As an open-access journal committed to equitable dissemination, there are no mandatory article processing charges for accepted papers in 2025 due to grant support from sponsoring institutions. Voluntary donations are welcome but not required.

8. Special Issues & Thematic Calls

The Journal periodically publishes special issues on emerging themes in AI ethics (e.g., “Alignment Problems: Technical Approaches & Moral Foundations”). Authors interested in contributing to special issues should consult current calls at https://journalofaie.org/calls-for-papers

9. Contact Information

Questions about submissions may be directed to editorial@journalofaie.org

10. Checklist Before Submission

Please ensure you have:
- Followed all formatting requirements  
- Included all required sections  
- Provided complete references  
- Disclosed conflicts of interest  
- Described data/code sharing procedures if applicable  
- Included a cover letter summarizing your manuscript’s fit with journal scope  

11. Example Topics Bridging Technical & Philosophical Analysis

To further clarify scope for interdisciplinary submissions—including alignment problems—the following examples illustrate suitable topics:
- Formal models for specifying moral values in machine learning systems alongside normative critique.
- Empirical investigations into unintended consequences of reinforcement learning agents with philosophical discussion of agency/responsibility.
- Case studies on real-world failures in algorithmic alignment accompanied by moral analysis.
- Proposals for integrating ethical theories into reward design mechanisms with theoretical justification.
If uncertain whether your topic fits journal scope, please contact us prior to submission.

Thank you for considering the Journal of AI Ethics as a venue for your work! We look forward to your contribution toward responsible innovation in artificial intelligence.

ECCV 2026 Tutorial Proposal Format Guidelines

This document provides detailed guidelines for preparing tutorial proposals for the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026. All tutorial proposals must strictly adhere to these requirements to ensure a fair and efficient review process.

I. GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS

1. Maximum Length:  
Tutorial proposals must not exceed four (4) pages, including references, figures, and tables. Proposals exceeding this limit will be returned without review.

2. Format:  
- Language: English  
- File format: PDF only  
- Font: Times New Roman, 11pt  
- Margins: At least 1 inch (2.54 cm) on all sides  
- Line spacing: Single  
- Page size: A4 or US Letter  

3. Submission:  
All proposals should be submitted via the ECCV 2026 Tutorial Proposal Submission Portal by the stated deadline. Late submissions will not be considered.

II. PROPOSAL STRUCTURE

Proposals must contain the following sections, in the order specified below:

A. Title Page (Required Information)
--------------------------------------
- Title of the proposed tutorial
- Names, affiliations, and contact information (email addresses) of all presenters
- Primary contact person for correspondence
- Preferred tutorial duration (half-day or full-day)
- Keywords (3–5 keywords relevant to the tutorial topic)

B. Abstract (Maximum 200 words)
-------------------------------
Provide a concise summary of the tutorial topic, objectives, and intended audience.

C. Motivation and Relevance
---------------------------
Explain why this tutorial is timely and important for ECCV attendees. Describe how it aligns with current trends in computer vision and related fields, and specify what makes it distinct from existing tutorials or courses.

D. Detailed Description of Content
----------------------------------
Outline the topics that will be covered in the tutorial in detail. Include a preliminary schedule with approximate time allocations for each major section or activity. If applicable, mention any hands-on sessions, demonstrations, or interactive components.

E. Intended Audience and Prerequisites
--------------------------------------
Describe the target audience (e.g., students, researchers, practitioners), their expected background knowledge, and any prerequisites required to benefit from the tutorial.

F. Presenter Information
------------------------
For each presenter:
- Full name
- Affiliation
- Short biography (up to 150 words per presenter)
- Relevant experience in teaching/tutorials and subject matter expertise

G. Previous Editions (if applicable)
------------------------------------
If this tutorial has been presented at previous conferences or venues, provide details including where and when it was offered, attendance numbers, feedback received, and any modifications planned for ECCV 2026.

H. Supporting Materials
-----------------------
List materials that will be provided to participants (e.g., slides, code samples, datasets). Indicate whether these materials will be publicly available after the event.

I. References
-------------
Include references to key publications related to the tutorial topic as well as prior work by the presenters.

III. REVIEW CRITERIA

Tutorial proposals will be evaluated based on:
- Relevance to ECCV and its community
- Timeliness and importance of the topic
- Quality and clarity of content description
- Expertise and experience of presenters
- Level of interest for expected attendees
- Balance across topics and avoidance of overlap with other tutorials

IV. TUTORIAL FORMAT AND LOGISTICS

1. Duration:
   - Half-day tutorials are typically scheduled for 3 hours (excluding breaks).
   - Full-day tutorials are scheduled for up to 6 hours (including breaks).
   - Please indicate your preferred duration in the proposal.

2. Presentation Mode:
   - Tutorials may be delivered in-person or in hybrid format depending on conference arrangements.
   - Please specify if you have special requirements for remote participation or technical setup.

3. Participant Engagement:
   - Proposals including interactive components such as Q&A sessions, hands-on exercises, group discussions, or live demonstrations are encouraged.
   - Please detail how you plan to engage participants during your session.

4. Materials Distribution:
   - Presenters are expected to provide slides and supplementary materials in advance for inclusion on the conference website.
   - Please confirm your willingness to share materials post-event if possible.

V. PRESENTER RESPONSIBILITIES

Selected tutorial presenters are expected to:
- Register for ECCV 2026 at least one presenter per accepted proposal.
- Coordinate with conference organizers regarding scheduling and logistics.
- Prepare high-quality presentation materials suitable for publication on the conference website.
- Adhere strictly to allocated time slots during their session.
- Respond promptly to communications from ECCV Tutorial Chairs.

VI. SUBMISSION CHECKLIST

Before submitting your proposal, please ensure:
[ ] The document does not exceed four pages.
[ ] All required sections are included in order.
[ ] Presenter biographies are concise and relevant.
[ ] The abstract clearly summarizes objectives and scope.
[ ] The schedule is outlined with time allocations.
[ ] References are complete and formatted consistently.
[ ] Contact information is accurate.
[ ] The PDF file is properly formatted according to specifications.

VII. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q1: Can I submit more than one tutorial proposal?
A1: Yes; however, each proposal must be unique and meet all requirements.

Q2: Is there financial support for presenters?
A2: Limited travel support may be available; details will be provided upon acceptance.

Q3: May I update my proposal after submission?
A3: Edits can be made until the submission deadline; after that no changes are allowed.

Q4: Will tutorials be recorded?
A4: Tutorials may be recorded subject to presenter consent; please indicate preferences in your proposal.

VIII. CONTACT INFORMATION

For questions regarding tutorial proposals or submission procedures, please contact:
ECCV 2026 Tutorial Chairs  
Email: tutorials@eccv2026.org

IX. IMPORTANT DATES

Proposal Submission Deadline: [to be announced]  
Notification of Acceptance: [to be announced]  
Final Materials Due: [to be announced]

X. SAMPLE OUTLINE FOR TUTORIAL PROPOSAL

Below is an example outline illustrating required sections:

---
Title: Advances in Self-Supervised Learning for Visual Recognition  
Presenters: Dr. Alice Smith (University X), Dr. Bob Lee (Institute Y)  
Contact Person: alice.smith@universityx.edu  
Preferred Duration: Half-day  
Keywords: self-supervised learning, visual recognition, deep learning

Abstract:
This tutorial introduces recent advances in self-supervised learning methods for visual recognition tasks...

Motivation and Relevance:
Self-supervised learning has emerged as a critical area within computer vision...

Detailed Description of Content:
The tutorial will cover theoretical foundations...

Intended Audience and Prerequisites:
Targeted at graduate students...

Presenter Information:
Dr. Alice Smith is an associate professor...

Previous Editions:
Presented at CVPR 2025...

Supporting Materials:
Slides, code samples...

References:
[1] Smith et al., "Self-Supervised Learning," IJCV 2024...
---

- Proposals focused on commercial products or proprietary technologies will not be considered unless they offer substantial scientific value.
- ECCV strongly encourages diversity among presenters regarding career stage, institution, geography, gender, etc.
- Collaborative tutorials spanning multiple institutions are welcome.

This policy applies to all manuscripts submitted to Pattern Recognition Letters that are based on or extend work previously published in peer-reviewed conference proceedings. The purpose of this policy is to ensure that extended versions represent significant advances over the original conference paper and provide added value to the scientific community.

2. Definition of Extended Version

An “extended version” refers to a manuscript submitted to PRL that builds upon work previously published in a conference proceeding. The extended version must offer substantial new content, including but not limited to new theoretical developments, additional experimental results, deeper analysis, or broader scope.

3. Minimum Requirements for New Content

To be considered for publication as an extended version, the manuscript must contain at least 30% new content compared to the original conference paper. The assessment of new content includes:

- New theoretical results or derivations
- Additional experiments or case studies
- Expanded discussions or insights
- Inclusion of new datasets or benchmarks
- Enhanced methodological details
- Significant improvements or modifications to the original approach

Authors should explicitly indicate in their cover letter and within the manuscript (typically as a footnote on the first page) which sections constitute new material and how these additions differ from the prior publication.

4. Originality and Plagiarism

All submissions must adhere to PRL’s standards for originality. Self-plagiarism, defined as verbatim or near-verbatim reuse of substantial portions of text without proper citation, is strictly prohibited. Authors must ensure that any reused material from the conference paper is appropriately cited, and that the extended version offers significant new contributions.

5. Disclosure Requirements

When submitting an extended version, authors are required to:

a) Clearly disclose in both the cover letter and within the manuscript that the submission is based on a previously published conference paper.

b) Provide full bibliographic details of the conference paper, including title, authors, venue, date of publication, and DOI (if available).

c) Submit a copy of the original conference paper as supplementary material during submission for comparison purposes.

d) Summarize in the cover letter and/or a dedicated section within the manuscript what constitutes new content (with approximate percentage), highlighting differences from the conference version.

6. Permissions and Copyright Considerations

It is the responsibility of authors to ensure compliance with copyright policies of both Pattern Recognition Letters and the publisher of the original conference proceedings. If any portion of text, figures, tables, or other materials from the original conference paper is reused in the extended version, authors must confirm that such reuse does not violate copyright agreements.

If required by the original publisher, authors must obtain written permission for reuse and submit proof during manuscript submission.

7. Peer Review Process

Extended versions will undergo PRL’s standard peer review process. Reviewers will be provided with both the submitted manuscript and the original conference paper(s) for comparison. Manuscripts will be evaluated based on:

- The degree and quality of new content
- Originality and significance of contributions
- Technical soundness
- Clarity of presentation
- Appropriateness for PRL’s scope

Submissions failing to meet the minimum requirement for new content (at least 30%) may be rejected without review.

Authors must properly cite their previous conference publication(s) throughout the manuscript wherever relevant content overlaps. Citations should follow PRL’s referencing style.

- Inclusion of additional experimental results using novel datasets or methods
- Expansion from a specific application domain in the conference paper to broader applicability demonstrated in PRL submission
- Significant theoretical advancements beyond those reported in the conference publication
- Comprehensive comparative studies with existing methods not present in prior work
- Integration of interdisciplinary perspectives leading to enhanced understanding or performance

- Mere expansion of background literature review without substantive technical advancement
- Minor editorial changes (e.g., improved grammar or language)
- Addition or modification of a small number of figures/tables without substantial analysis
- Superficial extension with limited incremental results lacking depth

Reviewer Report  
Manuscript Title: "Numerical Methods for Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations: An Adaptive Mesh Approach"  
Author: Dr. Maria Gomez  
Submission ID: JAM_2024_1123  
Date of Review: December 5, 2023

Reviewer Comments:

Summary:

This manuscript presents a novel adaptive mesh algorithm for the numerical solution of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), with applications to fluid dynamics and reaction-diffusion systems. The author proposes an approach that combines error estimation techniques with dynamic grid refinement, aiming to improve computational efficiency and accuracy compared to traditional uniform mesh methods. Several benchmark problems are considered, including the Navier-Stokes equations and Fisher-KPP equation, and the results are compared with existing finite difference and finite element schemes.

The topic is timely and relevant for readers of the Journal of Applied Mathematics. The paper is generally well-written, and the technical content is sound. However, there are several areas where clarification, additional details, and further validation would strengthen the manuscript. My detailed comments are below.

Major Comments:

1. Novelty and Contribution

The adaptive mesh strategy proposed in this work appears promising for improving computational performance in nonlinear PDE simulations. While the author provides a good overview of existing methods (Section 2), it would be beneficial to more clearly delineate how the present method advances beyond prior adaptive algorithms, especially those cited in [13], [16], and [22]. For example, is the error indicator fundamentally different from those previously used? What are the theoretical guarantees regarding convergence or stability? A comparative discussion with these works would help clarify the novelty.

2. Mathematical Formulation

Section 3 describes the adaptive mesh algorithm in detail; however, some aspects require clarification:

- The description of the error estimator (Equation 7) is somewhat brief. Please provide more intuition on its construction and why it is suitable for nonlinear problems.
- The grid refinement criterion (Algorithm 1) uses a threshold parameter ε. How sensitive are results to this choice? Have you performed any sensitivity analysis?
- The boundary treatment for adaptively refined meshes is not discussed. For problems like Navier-Stokes, how do you ensure boundary conditions remain well-posed as the mesh changes?

Providing more mathematical justification for key steps would strengthen confidence in the approach.

3. Numerical Experiments

The numerical experiments are comprehensive and address several important test cases. Nevertheless, I have several suggestions:

- Benchmark Selection: While the Fisher-KPP equation is a standard test case, consider including additional nonlinear reaction-diffusion models (e.g., FitzHugh-Nagumo) to further demonstrate robustness.
- Comparison Metrics: Table 2 reports L2 errors and CPU times for your method versus standard finite difference schemes. It would be useful to also compare against adaptive finite element methods if possible, as these are commonly used in practice.
- Scalability: Have you tested your algorithm on larger-scale problems or parallel implementations? Some discussion on scalability would be valuable for readers interested in high-performance computing applications.

4. Validation

For the Navier-Stokes benchmarks (Section 4.2), you compare numerical results to reference solutions from [28]. It would be helpful to include plots showing both qualitative agreement (e.g., velocity profiles) and quantitative error norms over time. ECCV 2026 Supplementary Material Guidelines

This document outlines the requirements and recommendations for preparing supplementary materials for submissions to ECCV 2026. Please read these guidelines carefully to ensure your supplementary files comply with the conference’s policies.

1. Purpose of Supplementary Materials

Supplementary materials are intended to provide additional content that supports and enhances the main paper submission. They may include:

- Additional experimental results
- Detailed descriptions of algorithms or proofs omitted due to space constraints
- Visualizations (e.g., video demonstrations)
- Extended tables, figures, or datasets
- Source code (if allowed by the track; see Section 7)

Supplementary materials are optional but encouraged where they provide meaningful additional information for reviewers.

2. Allowed File Formats

For ECCV 2026, only the following file formats are accepted for supplementary materials:

- PDF (.pdf): For textual, tabular, or graphical content such as appendices, extended results, figures, and explanations.
- MP4 (.mp4): For video demonstrations or visualizations.

No other formats will be accepted. Do not submit ZIP archives, Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, or other file types. If your supplementary content includes multiple items (e.g., several figures and tables), please compile them into a single PDF file.

3. Maximum File Size

The total size of all supplementary material submitted per paper must not exceed 100MB.

Submissions exceeding this limit will be rejected by the system. It is recommended to optimize your files (compress images in PDFs, use reasonable video encoding settings) to stay within this limit while maintaining clarity and readability.

4. Submission Instructions

a) Upload Procedure

During the paper submission process via the ECCV 2026 submission portal, you will be prompted to upload supplementary material after submitting your main paper PDF.

b) Naming Convention

Please use the following naming convention for your supplementary files:

- [PaperID]_supplementary.pdf
- [PaperID]_supplementary.mp4

Replace [PaperID] with your assigned submission ID (e.g., 1234_supplementary.pdf).

If submitting both PDF and MP4 files, upload each separately using the above convention.

c) Deadlines

Supplementary material must be uploaded before the main paper submission deadline. Late submissions of supplementary files will not be considered.

5. Content Guidelines

a) Review Process

All supplementary material will be made available to reviewers alongside your main submission. Reviewers are not required to review supplementary content in detail but may consult it at their discretion.

Do not include any information in the supplementary material that is essential for understanding the core contributions of your paper; such information should appear in the main manuscript.

b) Anonymity and Double-Blind Review

ECCV 2026 uses double-blind review. Ensure that all supplementary files are anonymized:

- Do not include author names, affiliations, acknowledgments, or explicit self-references.
- Remove metadata from PDFs and MP4s that could identify authors.
- Avoid mentioning links to personal websites or repositories that would compromise anonymity during review.

Any violation of anonymity requirements may result in desk rejection.

c) Appropriate Content

Examples of appropriate supplementary content:

- Additional experimental results (e.g., more test cases, full ablation studies)
- Extended mathematical derivations
- High-resolution versions of key figures/tables
- Video demonstrations of system behavior or qualitative results (MP4 format only)
- Pseudocode or algorithmic details not included in the main paper due to length constraints

Examples of inappropriate content:

- Main paper text that should have been included in the primary submission
- Promotional material
- Non-anonymized references or acknowledgments
- Unrelated data or excessive raw data dumps

6. Preparation Tips

a) PDF Preparation

- Use standard fonts and formatting.
- Ensure figures and tables are readable at typical screen resolutions.
- Compress images appropriately to reduce file size without losing essential detail.
- Check for broken links or missing resources before submission.
- Remove all identifying metadata from the document properties.

b) MP4 Preparation

- Recommended resolution: 720p (1280x720) or lower unless higher resolution is essential.
- Use widely supported codecs (H.264 recommended).
- Limit video length: Reviewers appreciate concise demonstrations (suggested maximum duration: 5 minutes).
- Avoid including spoken commentary that could reveal identities; use captions if necessary.
- Test playback on multiple platforms before submission.

7. Code Submission Policy

At present, ECCV 2026 does **not** accept source code as part of supplementary materials unless explicitly requested by a track chair for specific tracks. If code submission is allowed:

- Include code only as part of a PDF appendix (do not upload .zip or .tar archives).
- Anonymize code comments and filenames.
- Do **not** link to external repositories in a way that compromises anonymity.

Please check specific track instructions if you believe your submission falls under an exception.

8. Copyright and Third-party Material

Authors must ensure they have rights to share all content included in supplementary materials. Do not include copyrighted material without appropriate permissions (e.g., videos from third parties).

9. Accessibility Considerations

ECCV encourages authors to make supplementary materials accessible:

PDFs:
 - Use readable fonts and clear layouts.
 - Add alt-text descriptions for important figures when possible.

Videos:
 - Provide captions for spoken dialogue if present.
 - Ensure color contrasts are sufficient for viewers with color vision deficiencies.

10. Post-Acceptance Policy

If your paper is accepted, you may be invited to submit additional non-anonymized supplementary material for public release alongside the camera-ready version. You will receive further instructions at that stage.

11. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q: Can I submit more than one PDF or MP4?
A: You may submit one PDF and/or one MP4 file per paper. Multiple files of each type are not permitted; combine contents into a single file per format if needed.

Q: What happens if my file exceeds 100MB?
A: The system will reject uploads over 100MB total size per paper; compress files as needed before uploading.

Q: Can I update my supplementary material after submission?
A: Supplementary material must be finalized before the submission deadline; changes are not permitted after this point except under exceptional circumstances as approved by program chairs.

Q: May I reference my own previous work in supplementary materials?
A: Yes, but do so in a manner consistent with double-blind review—refer to yourself in the third person and avoid revealing identities through citations or phrasing.

Q: Is it mandatory to submit supplementary material?
A: No, it is optional. However, high-quality supplementary material can aid reviewers’ understanding of your work.

12. Contact Information

For technical issues regarding uploading files or questions about these guidelines, contact the ECCV 2026 Submission Committee at eccv2026-support@conference.org.

13. Summary Checklist Before Submission

Before uploading your supplementary materials, please verify:

[ ] My files are in PDF and/or MP4 format only.
[ ] Total size does not exceed 100MB.
[ ] All content is anonymized—no names, affiliations, acknowledgments.
[ ] No essential information has been placed solely in supplementary material.
[ ] I have checked accessibility considerations where possible.
[ ] My files follow naming conventions as specified above.
[ ] I have removed identifying metadata from all files.
[ ] All content complies with copyright requirements.

Thank you for adhering to these guidelines and contributing to a smooth review process at ECCV 2026!

This document outlines the requirements and recommendations for preparing supplementary materials for submissions to ECCV 2026. Please read these guidelines carefully to ensure your supplementary files comply with the conference’s policies.

1. Purpose of Supplementary Materials

Supplementary materials are intended to provide additional content that supports and enhances the main paper submission. They may include:

- Additional experimental results
- Detailed descriptions of algorithms or proofs omitted due to space constraints
- Visualizations (e.g., video demonstrations)
- Extended tables, figures, or datasets
- Source code (if allowed by the track; see Section 7)

Supplementary materials are optional but encouraged where they provide meaningful additional information for reviewers.

2. Allowed File Formats

For ECCV 2026, only the following file formats are accepted for supplementary materials:

- PDF (.pdf): For textual, tabular, or graphical content such as appendices, extended results, figures, and explanations.
- MP4 (.mp4): For video demonstrations or visualizations.

No other formats will be accepted. Do not submit ZIP archives, Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, or other file types. If your supplementary content includes multiple items (e.g., several figures and tables), please compile them into a single PDF file.

3. Maximum File Size

The total size of all supplementary material submitted per paper must not exceed 100MB.

Submissions exceeding this limit will be rejected by the system. It is recommended to optimize your files (compress images in PDFs, use reasonable video encoding settings) to stay within this limit while maintaining clarity and readability.

4. Submission Instructions

a) Upload Procedure

During the paper submission process via the ECCV 2026 submission portal, you will be prompted to upload supplementary material after submitting your main paper PDF.

b) Naming Convention

Please use the following naming convention for your supplementary files:

- [PaperID]_supplementary.pdf
- [PaperID]_supplementary.mp4

Replace [PaperID] with your assigned submission ID (e.g., 1234_supplementary.pdf).

If submitting both PDF and MP4 files, upload each separately using the above convention.

c) Deadlines

Supplementary material must be uploaded before the main paper submission deadline. Late submissions of supplementary files will not be considered.

5. Content Guidelines

a) Review Process

All supplementary material will be made available to reviewers alongside your main submission. Reviewers are not required to review supplementary content in detail but may consult it at their discretion.

Do not include any information in the supplementary material that is essential for understanding the core contributions of your paper; such information should appear in the main manuscript.

b) Anonymity and Double-Blind Review

ECCV 2026 uses double-blind review. Ensure that all supplementary files are anonymized:

- Do not include author names, affiliations, acknowledgments, or explicit self-references.
- Remove metadata from PDFs and MP4s that could identify authors.
- Avoid mentioning links to personal websites or repositories that would compromise anonymity during review.

Any violation of anonymity requirements may result in desk rejection.

c) Appropriate Content

Examples of appropriate supplementary content:

- Additional experimental results (e.g., more test cases, full ablation studies)
- Extended mathematical derivations
- High-resolution versions of key figures/tables
- Video demonstrations of system behavior or qualitative results (MP4 format only)
- Pseudocode or algorithmic details not included in the main paper due to length constraints

Examples of inappropriate content:

- Main paper text that should have been included in the primary submission
- Promotional material
- Non-anonymized references or acknowledgments
- Unrelated data or excessive raw data dumps

6. Preparation Tips

a) PDF Preparation

- Use standard fonts and formatting.
- Ensure figures and tables are readable at typical screen resolutions.
- Compress images appropriately to reduce file size without losing essential detail.
- Check for broken links or missing resources before submission.
- Remove all identifying metadata from the document properties.

b) MP4 Preparation

- Recommended resolution: 720p (1280x720) or lower unless higher resolution is essential.
- Use widely supported codecs (H.264 recommended).
- Limit video length: Reviewers appreciate concise demonstrations (suggested maximum duration: 5 minutes).
- Avoid including spoken commentary that could reveal identities; use captions if necessary.
- Test playback on multiple platforms before submission.

7. Code Submission Policy

At present, ECCV 2026 does **not** accept source code as part of supplementary materials unless explicitly requested by a track chair for specific tracks. If code submission is allowed:

- Include code only as part of a PDF appendix (do not upload .zip or .tar archives).
- Anonymize code comments and filenames.
- Do **not** link to external repositories in a way that compromises anonymity.

Please check specific track instructions if you believe your submission falls under an exception.

8. Copyright and Third-party Material

Authors must ensure they have rights to share all content included in supplementary materials. Do not include copyrighted material without appropriate permissions (e.g., videos from third parties).

9. Accessibility Considerations

ECCV encourages authors to make supplementary materials accessible:

PDFs:
 - Use readable fonts and clear layouts.
 - Add alt-text descriptions for important figures when possible.

Videos:
 - Provide captions for spoken dialogue if present.
 - Ensure color contrasts are sufficient for viewers with color vision deficiencies.

10. Post-Acceptance Policy

If your paper is accepted, you may be invited to submit additional non-anonymized supplementary material for public release alongside the camera-ready version. You will receive further instructions at that stage.

11. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q: Can I submit more than one PDF or MP4?
A: You may submit one PDF and/or one MP4 file per paper. Multiple files of each type are not permitted; combine contents into a single file per format if needed.

Q: What happens if my file exceeds 100MB?
A: The system will reject uploads over 100MB total size per paper; compress files as needed before uploading.

Q: Can I update my supplementary material after submission?
A: Supplementary material must be finalized before the submission deadline; changes are not permitted after this point except under exceptional circumstances as approved by program chairs.

Q: May I reference my own previous work in supplementary materials?
A: Yes, but do so in a manner consistent with double-blind review—refer to yourself in the third person and avoid revealing identities through citations or phrasing.

Q: Is it mandatory to submit supplementary material?
A: No, it is optional. However, high-quality supplementary material can aid reviewers’ understanding of your work.

12. Contact Information

For technical issues regarding uploading files or questions about these guidelines, contact the ECCV 2026 Submission Committee at eccv2026-support@conference.org.

13. Summary Checklist Before Submission

Before uploading your supplementary materials, please verify:

[ ] My files are in PDF and/or MP4 format only.
[ ] Total size does not exceed 100MB.
[ ] All content is anonymized—no names, affiliations, acknowledgments.
[ ] No essential information has been placed solely in supplementary material.
[ ] I have checked accessibility considerations where possible.
[ ] My files follow naming conventions as specified above.
[ ] I have removed identifying metadata from all files.
[ ] All content complies with copyright requirements.

Thank you for adhering to these guidelines and contributing to a smooth review process at ECCV 2026!

ECCV 2026 Submission Committee

NeurIPS 2025 ML4Sec Workshop  
Paper Format Instructions

This document provides formatting guidelines for papers submitted to the NeurIPS 2025 “Machine Learning for Cybersecurity” (ML4Sec) workshop. Authors are required to follow these instructions in addition to using the official NeurIPS 2025 style file/template. Please read carefully before preparing your submission.

---

**1. General Formatting**

All submissions must use the NeurIPS 2025 LaTeX style file, available from the main conference website (https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/PaperInformation/StyleFiles). Both PDF and source files (LaTeX) must be submitted.

- **Page Size:** US Letter (8.5 x 11 inches).
- **Font:** Use Times New Roman or Computer Modern fonts, as per the template.
- **Font Size:** Main text should be 10-point font.
- **Margins:** As set by the official style file; do not modify margins.
- **Line Spacing:** Single-spaced.
- **Columns:** Two-column format is mandatory.

---

**2. Length of Submissions**

Workshop papers should adhere to the following length restrictions:

- **Maximum Length:** 7 pages of main content, including figures, tables, and references.
- **References:** References must fit within the 7-page limit. No extra pages for references.
- **Appendices/Supplementary Material:** Optional appendices may be included after the main paper and references. There is no strict page limit on appendices, but reviewers are not required to read them.

---

**3. Title and Author Information**

- The title should appear at the top of the first page, in boldface and centered.
- Author names and affiliations should be listed below the title, as per template.
- For multiple authors, use superscripted numbers or symbols to indicate affiliations if needed.
- Indicate corresponding author with an asterisk (*), if desired.

---

**4. Abstract**

Include an abstract of up to 250 words at the beginning of the paper, formatted according to the template instructions.

---

**5. Keywords**

List up to five keywords below the abstract to aid in reviewer assignment.

---

**6. Figures and Tables**

- Place figures and tables within the body of the paper near where they are first referenced.
- All figures must have descriptive captions.
- Ensure that all images are high-resolution and readable when printed in black-and-white.
- Avoid using color as the sole means of conveying information; use patterns or shapes where possible.

---

**7. Citations and References**

Use BibTeX for citations if submitting LaTeX source files. All references must be cited in-text and listed in the references section at the end of the paper.

- Follow NeurIPS citation style: numbered or author-year formats are both acceptable.
- Hyperlinks for URLs should be included where relevant (e.g., code repositories).

---

**8. Anonymity**

The ML4Sec workshop uses single-blind review:

- Author names and affiliations SHOULD be included in submissions.
- Do NOT anonymize your manuscript.

---

**9. Supplementary Materials**

Authors may submit supplementary materials such as proofs, additional experiments, datasets, or code:

- Supplementary material should be clearly marked as such and placed after references.
- Clearly reference supplementary items in the main text (e.g., “see Appendix A”).
- There is no strict page limit for supplementary material, but conciseness is encouraged.

---

**10. Reproducibility Checklist**

To promote reproducibility, we encourage authors to include a reproducibility checklist as an appendix. The checklist can cover:

- Dataset availability (include links if public)
- Code availability
- Description of experimental setup
- Details on hyperparameters
- Statistical significance testing

This checklist is optional but strongly encouraged.

---

**11. Ethical Considerations Statement**

Given the sensitive nature of cybersecurity research, authors are encouraged to include an ethical considerations statement at the end of their paper or in an appendix. This statement should discuss any potential risks associated with publication or deployment of methods described in your work.

Topics you may wish to address:

- Dual-use concerns (e.g., offensive security applications)
- Data privacy issues
- Responsible disclosure practices
- Societal impact

If your work does not raise any ethical concerns, please briefly state this.

---

**12. Submission Instructions**

All papers must be submitted via CMT (Conference Management Toolkit) through the workshop’s submission portal: [link will be provided on workshop webpage].

Required submission materials:

1. PDF version of your manuscript
2. Source files (.tex/.bib/.pdf)
3. Supplementary material (if any)

Ensure that your PDF compiles correctly and adheres to formatting requirements before submission.

---

**13. Review Criteria**

Papers will be evaluated based on:

- Originality and novelty
- Technical soundness
- Relevance to machine learning for cybersecurity
- Clarity of presentation
- Reproducibility
- Ethical considerations

Submissions that do not follow formatting guidelines may be desk rejected without review.

---

**14. Camera-ready Instructions (for Accepted Papers)**

If your paper is accepted for presentation or inclusion in workshop proceedings:

1. Revise your manuscript based on reviewer feedback.
2. Ensure all formatting complies with these instructions and with NeurIPS style guidelines.
3. Upload final PDF and source files by camera-ready deadline (to be announced).
4. Provide a short video summary (optional; details will be sent post-review).

Accepted papers will be made publicly available via OpenReview or similar platform unless otherwise stated.

---

**15. Presentation Format**

Authors of accepted papers will be invited for either oral presentations or poster sessions during the workshop day at NeurIPS 2025.

Presentation guidelines will be sent upon acceptance; typical formats include:

- Oral talks: 10–15 minutes + Q&A
- Posters: A0 size recommended

Remote presentations may be supported subject to conference policies.

---

**16. Paper Withdrawal Policy**

Authors wishing to withdraw their submission must notify workshop chairs before review begins by email ([workshop contact email]).

After review starts, withdrawal requests may not always be honored depending on review stage.

---

**17. Accessibility Guidelines**

Please ensure that your manuscript is accessible to all readers:

- Use sufficiently large font sizes in figures/tables.
- Avoid color combinations problematic for colorblind readers.
- Add alt-text descriptions to images if possible.

For more tips on accessibility, consult https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/PaperInformation/AccessibilityGuidelines

---

**18. Frequently Asked Questions**

_Q: May I submit work that has appeared elsewhere?_  
A: Workshop submissions may present preliminary work, extensions of published research, or papers under consideration elsewhere provided there are no copyright conflicts and you disclose previous dissemination in your cover letter.

_Q: Is dual submission allowed?_  
A: Dual submissions are permitted only if they comply with copyright restrictions and are disclosed at submission time.

_Q: Can I submit extended abstracts?_  
A: Yes; however, extended abstracts must still comply with formatting rules above (maximum 7 pages including references).

_Q: Are non-academic submissions welcome?_  
A: Yes! We encourage industry practitioners and students to submit applied work relevant to machine learning for cybersecurity.

_Q: What about non-LaTeX submissions?_  
A: We strongly recommend LaTeX for consistency but will accept Word manuscripts if formatted identically to NeurIPS style (template available upon request).

---

**19. Contact Information**

For questions regarding paper format or submission process, please contact us at [workshop contact email]. For technical issues with CMT portal, see help documentation on CMT website.

For updates on deadlines or format changes, refer to our workshop website [URL].

NeurIPS 2025 ML4Sec Workshop  
Paper Format Instructions

This document provides formatting guidelines for papers submitted to the NeurIPS 2025 “Machine Learning for Cybersecurity” (ML4Sec) workshop. Authors are required to follow these instructions in addition to using the official NeurIPS 2025 style file/template. Please read carefully before preparing your submission.

---

**1. General Formatting**

All submissions must use the NeurIPS 2025 LaTeX style file, available from the main conference website (https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/PaperInformation/StyleFiles). Both PDF and source files (LaTeX) must be submitted.

- **Page Size:** US Letter (8.5 x 11 inches).
- **Font:** Use Times New Roman or Computer Modern fonts, as per the template.
- **Font Size:** Main text should be 10-point font.
- **Margins:** As set by the official style file; do not modify margins.
- **Line Spacing:** Single-spaced.
- **Columns:** Two-column format is mandatory.

---

**2. Length of Submissions**

Workshop papers should adhere to the following length restrictions:

- **Maximum Length:** 7 pages of main content, including figures, tables, and references.
- **References:** References must fit within the 7-page limit. No extra pages for references.
- **Appendices/Supplementary Material:** Optional appendices may be included after the main paper and references. There is no strict page limit on appendices, but reviewers are not required to read them.

---

**3. Title and Author Information**

- The title should appear at the top of the first page, in boldface and centered.
- Author names and affiliations should be listed below the title, as per template.
- For multiple authors, use superscripted numbers or symbols to indicate affiliations if needed.
- Indicate corresponding author with an asterisk (*), if desired.

---

**4. Abstract**

Include an abstract of up to 250 words at the beginning of the paper, formatted according to the template instructions.

---

**5. Keywords**

List up to five keywords below the abstract to aid in reviewer assignment.

---

**6. Figures and Tables**

- Place figures and tables within the body of the paper near where they are first referenced.
- All figures must have descriptive captions.
- Ensure that all images are high-resolution and readable when printed in black-and-white.
- Avoid using color as the sole means of conveying information; use patterns or shapes where possible.

---

**7. Citations and References**

Use BibTeX for citations if submitting LaTeX source files. All references must be cited in-text and listed in the references section at the end of the paper.

- Follow NeurIPS citation style: numbered or author-year formats are both acceptable.
- Hyperlinks for URLs should be included where relevant (e.g., code repositories).

---

**8. Anonymity**

The ML4Sec workshop uses single-blind review:

- Author names and affiliations SHOULD be included in submissions.
- Do NOT anonymize your manuscript.

---

**9. Supplementary Materials**

Authors may submit supplementary materials such as proofs, additional experiments, datasets, or code:

- Supplementary material should be clearly marked as such and placed after references.
- Clearly reference supplementary items in the main text (e.g., “see Appendix A”).
- There is no strict page limit for supplementary material, but conciseness is encouraged.

---

**10. Reproducibility Checklist**

To promote reproducibility, we encourage authors to include a reproducibility checklist as an appendix. The checklist can cover:

- Dataset availability (include links if public)
- Code availability
- Description of experimental setup
- Details on hyperparameters
- Statistical significance testing

This checklist is optional but strongly encouraged.

---

**11. Ethical Considerations Statement**

Given the sensitive nature of cybersecurity research, authors are encouraged to include an ethical considerations statement at the end of their paper or in an appendix. This statement should discuss any potential risks associated with publication or deployment of methods described in your work.

Topics you may wish to address:

- Dual-use concerns (e.g., offensive security applications)
- Data privacy issues
- Responsible disclosure practices
- Societal impact

If your work does not raise any ethical concerns, please briefly state this.

---

**12. Submission Instructions**

All papers must be submitted via CMT (Conference Management Toolkit) through the workshop’s submission portal: [link will be provided on workshop webpage].

Required submission materials:

1. PDF version of your manuscript
2. Source files (.tex/.bib/.pdf)
3. Supplementary material (if any)

Ensure that your PDF compiles correctly and adheres to formatting requirements before submission.

---

**13. Review Criteria**

Papers will be evaluated based on:

- Originality and novelty
- Technical soundness
- Relevance to machine learning for cybersecurity
- Clarity of presentation
- Reproducibility
- Ethical considerations

Submissions that do not follow formatting guidelines may be desk rejected without review.

---

**14. Camera-ready Instructions (for Accepted Papers)**

If your paper is accepted for presentation or inclusion in workshop proceedings:

1. Revise your manuscript based on reviewer feedback.
2. Ensure all formatting complies with these instructions and with NeurIPS style guidelines.
3. Upload final PDF and source files by camera-ready deadline (to be announced).
4. Provide a short video summary (optional; details will be sent post-review).

Accepted papers will be made publicly available via OpenReview or similar platform unless otherwise stated.

---

**15. Presentation Format**

Authors of accepted papers will be invited for either oral presentations or poster sessions during the workshop day at NeurIPS 2025.

Presentation guidelines will be sent upon acceptance; typical formats include:

- Oral talks: 10–15 minutes + Q&A
- Posters: A0 size recommended

Remote presentations may be supported subject to conference policies.

---

**16. Paper Withdrawal Policy**

Authors wishing to withdraw their submission must notify workshop chairs before review begins by email ([workshop contact email]).

After review starts, withdrawal requests may not always be honored depending on review stage.

---

**17. Accessibility Guidelines**

Please ensure that your manuscript is accessible to all readers:

- Use sufficiently large font sizes in figures/tables.
- Avoid color combinations problematic for colorblind readers.
- Add alt-text descriptions to images if possible.

For more tips on accessibility, consult https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/PaperInformation/AccessibilityGuidelines

---

**18. Frequently Asked Questions**

_Q: May I submit work that has appeared elsewhere?_  
A: Workshop submissions may present preliminary work, extensions of published research, or papers under consideration elsewhere provided there are no copyright conflicts and you disclose previous dissemination in your cover letter.

_Q: Is dual submission allowed?_  
A: Dual submissions are permitted only if they comply with copyright restrictions and are disclosed at submission time.

_Q: Can I submit extended abstracts?_  
A: Yes; however, extended abstracts must still comply with formatting rules above (maximum 7 pages including references).

_Q: Are non-academic submissions welcome?_  
A: Yes! We encourage industry practitioners and students to submit applied work relevant to machine learning for cybersecurity.

_Q: What about non-LaTeX submissions?_  
A: We strongly recommend LaTeX for consistency but will accept Word manuscripts if formatted identically to NeurIPS style (template available upon request).

---

**19. Contact Information**

For questions regarding paper format or submission process, please contact us at [workshop contact email]. For technical issues with CMT portal, see help documentation on CMT website.

For updates on deadlines or format changes, refer to our workshop website [URL].

---

Thank you for your interest in submitting to NeurIPS 2025 ML4Sec Workshop!

Workshop Chairs  
NeurIPS 2025 ML4Sec

Preprint Policy Statement  
Effective January 2025

1. Introduction

The ACM Transactions on AI (ACM TAI) recognizes the evolving landscape of scientific publishing and the increasing importance of preprints in promoting rapid dissemination and open access to research. This policy statement outlines ACM TAI’s position on preprints, including definitions, posting guidelines, citation practices, and implications for manuscript submission and review.

2. Definition of Preprints

A “preprint” is defined as a scholarly manuscript authored by researchers that has not yet undergone formal peer review and has not been accepted or published by a journal. Preprints are typically made publicly available on non-commercial repositories such as arXiv.org, bioRxiv.org, or similar platforms prior to, or concurrent with, submission to a journal for consideration.

3. Scope of Policy

This policy applies to all manuscripts submitted to ACM Transactions on AI after January 1, 2025. It governs the posting of preprints during the editorial review process and after acceptance for publication.

4. Posting Preprints Prior to Submission

Authors are permitted and encouraged to post their manuscripts as preprints prior to submission to ACM TAI. Preprints should be posted on reputable non-commercial public repositories that provide persistent identifiers (e.g., DOIs or arXiv IDs), ensure long-term access, and clearly label the status of the manuscript as “not peer-reviewed.”

Posting a preprint prior to submission does not affect eligibility for consideration at ACM TAI. Authors must disclose any preprint postings at the time of manuscript submission.

5. Posting Preprints During Peer Review

Authors may post or update preprints while their manuscript is under review at ACM TAI. The following conditions apply:

a) The preprint must be identical or substantially similar to the version submitted to ACM TAI.
b) The repository must clearly indicate that the manuscript is under consideration at ACM Transactions on AI.
c) Authors must notify the editorial office of any new postings or updates during the review process.
d) Any substantive changes made in response to reviewer comments should be updated in the preprint only after the revision has been formally submitted to ACM TAI.

6. Posting Preprints After Acceptance

Once a manuscript has been accepted for publication at ACM TAI, authors may update their preprint with an “accepted version.” However, they must adhere to copyright and licensing requirements as outlined in Section 9 below. Authors are encouraged to link the preprint to the final published article using its DOI once available.

7. Citation of Preprints in Manuscripts

Authors may cite relevant preprints within their submissions to ACM TAI provided that:

a) The cited preprint is publicly accessible via a recognized repository.
b) The citation includes sufficient information for identification (author(s), title, repository name, identifier such as DOI or arXiv ID, year).
c) The citation explicitly notes that it refers to a preprint (e.g., “arXiv preprint”).

Reviewers will be instructed to treat cited preprints appropriately and not penalize authors for citing work that has not yet undergone peer review.

8. Reviewer Guidance Regarding Preprints

ACM TAI reviewers are reminded that:

a) The presence of a publicly posted preprint does not constitute prior publication nor grounds for rejection.
b) Reviewers must evaluate the submitted manuscript independently of any public comments or feedback received via preprint repositories.
c) Anonymous peer review remains intact; reviewers should not seek out author identities via preprint platforms if double-blind review is in place.

9. Copyright and Licensing Considerations

a) Authors retain copyright over their posted preprints unless otherwise agreed with the repository.
b) Upon acceptance at ACM TAI, authors will be required to sign an appropriate copyright transfer agreement or license-to-publish arrangement with ACM.
c) Posting the “accepted version” (post-peer-review but before typesetting) is allowed provided it is labeled appropriately and links back to the published article when available.
d) Posting the final publisher-formatted PDF (“version of record”) is prohibited unless specifically permitted by ACM’s open access policies.

10. Embargoes and Publicity

There are no embargo restrictions on posting preprints before or during submission/review at ACM TAI. Authors may discuss their work publicly (e.g., conferences, media interviews), but should clarify that findings are preliminary if based solely on non-peer-reviewed versions.

11. Conflicts with Other Policies

If authors have previously posted their work as a preprint elsewhere (including institutional repositories), this does not violate ACM TAI’s originality requirement so long as:

a) The work has not been published in a peer-reviewed journal or proceedings,
b) The content matches what is submitted,
c) Disclosure is made at time of submission.

If submitting work previously posted as a conference paper, please refer to ACM’s conference-journal overlap policies.

12. Disclosure Requirements

During submission, authors must provide:

a) The URL/identifier of any relevant preprints,
b) A statement confirming that no peer-reviewed publication exists,
c) Notification of any subsequent updates during review.

Failure to disclose relevant preprints may result in delays in processing or withdrawal from consideration.

13. Handling Comments and Feedback on Preprints

Authors who receive public comments or feedback via preprint servers are welcome to incorporate constructive input into revised submissions. However, revisions in response to reviewer feedback should be prioritized over public commentary during peer review.

14. Benefits and Risks of Preprinting

ACM TAI recognizes several benefits associated with posting preprints:

- Accelerated dissemination of research findings
- Increased visibility and citations
- Opportunities for early feedback from peers
- Establishment of priority for novel results

However, authors should also consider potential risks:

- Exposure of errors prior to peer review
- Risk of being scooped if others build upon unreviewed results
- Potential confusion between preliminary findings and final published versions

Authors are encouraged to weigh these factors when deciding whether and when to post a preprint.

15. Open Access Considerations

Preprinting does not affect eligibility for open access publication at ACM TAI. Authors wishing to pursue Gold Open Access should consult ACM’s Author Rights page for details regarding Article Processing Charges (APCs), licensing options (e.g., CC BY), and permitted sharing formats.

16. Compliance with Funder Mandates

Many funding agencies require public access to research outputs via repositories such as arXiv or PubMed Central. Posting a preprint generally satisfies most funder mandates regarding early dissemination but does not substitute for compliance with open access requirements post-publication unless explicitly permitted by the funder.
